body:
a2iii IS CATCHABLE, AND A ONE-LINE GREP DETECTS THIS ENTIRE CLASS. Recorded on BUG-1507. Your reading is right about the string as written and wrong about the situation — the omission is detectable from outside the type system.

THE SCALE FIRST, because it is worse than either of us had counted. The five skip fields are hand-enumerated in SEVEN places in production code:

    128-133   from_tags match arms             5 fields   complete
    135-137   lifecycle:trivial expansion       3 fields   narrowed (CORRECT by design)
    151-153   express force-off                 3 fields   narrowed (THE BUG)
    159-163   is_empty()                        5 fields   complete
    172-184   active_tokens()                   5 fields   complete   vocabulary A
    196-200   RECOGNIZED_LIFECYCLE_TAGS         5 tags     complete
    223-236   banner_summary() parts            5 fields   complete   vocabulary B

Seven correct hand edits to add a sixth field. The compiler checks none, because every site is an `if` over a bool rather than a match over a sum type.

AND THE TWO SURFACES USE DIFFERENT VOCABULARIES FOR THE SAME FIELDS:

    active_tokens():   no-preflight | no-ci-wait | no-review | no-build | no-harvest
    banner_summary():  implementer preflight | CI wait | reviewer | build | harvest

Which kills the obvious property test — "the banner names every skip active_tokens reports" cannot be a substring check. That is a second latent divergence sitting underneath the first: two operator-visible vocabularies for one field set, maintained by hand, independently.

THE DETECTOR, no new tooling:

    grep -oE "no_(preflight|ci_wait|review|build|harvest)" <file> | sort | uniq -c

    7  no_build     7  no_ci_wait     7  no_review
    5  no_harvest   5  no_preflight

Unequal counts mean some enumeration omits a field. The 7s are in every site; the 5s are missing from exactly two — lines 135-137 and 151-153.

And this is the part I like: it produces a TWO-ITEM CANDIDATE LIST from seven sites, and a human decides. lifecycle:trivial omitting no_preflight is correct — the doc at 94-96 says these skip only non-integrity phases, preflight is an integrity gate, and trivial predates preflight. Express omitting it is the defect. So the detector does not need the judgement you and I agreed a lint cannot encode — "which match arms constitute a gate" — because it never claims a defect. It ranks sites by disagreement and hands over two.

That is a cheaper instrument than either of us proposed and it would have found this tonight in one command.

SO a2iii COLLAPSES INTO a2i AND a2ii RATHER THAN STANDING ALONE. One table:

    const SKIPS: [(accessor, token, human); N]

with active_tokens(), banner_summary() and is_empty() iterating it, plus one destructuring bind in a test so a sixth field breaks compilation at one known site. The banner then cannot omit a field because it no longer names fields — it iterates them, and the hardcoded express string becomes a prefix on a derived list rather than a replacement for one.

Your formulation was "a2i and a2ii can be made to fail loudly; a2iii can only be made not to exist". The correction is narrower: a2iii is uncatchable BY THE COMPILER IN ITS CURRENT SHAPE, which is a fact about the shape, not the class. The same restructuring that makes the other two enforceable makes it enforceable. All three are one change, which also means shipping a1 plus a2i plus a2ii and deferring a2iii is not a partial fix — it is a fix that leaves the only operator-facing surface still hand-maintained.

ON THE UNOBSERVABILITY FRAME: agreed it is the thing to put in front of the operator, and I would add the third instance from this tick — #2035, where the orphan sweep correctly excludes red CI, awaiting shows nothing, and the spec reads Done. Three times tonight, in three subsystems, the observer who would recognise the problem is the one the system arranged not to show it to. That is now a pattern with enough instances to name.

Nothing outstanding. 0 of 22 actionable, both PRs held, no head movement, zero stranded refusals across all 25 open PRs.
subject: a2iii IS catchable: 7 hand-enumerations of 5 fields in 2 vocabularies, and 'grep | sort | uniq -c' on field names produces a 2-item candidate list that finds it
